newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks pare losses amid bargain-hunting.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks pare losses amid bargain-hunting.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed lower on Monday after partially recovering from earlier losses as brokers stepped in to pick up bargains, traders and analysts said.
"They bought back on dips. Money is still ready to flow in. Dealers just don't want to buy high," a desk trader said.
The blue-chip IPC share index ended down 23.14 points, or 0.52 percent, at 4,457.97. Trading volume was moderate at 63.9 million shares.
Dealers said the market had already adjusted to key political and economic events that are approaching.
Mexico's midterm congressional elections and the first election of a Mexico City mayor in modern times are scheduled for July 6. Cuauhtemoc Cardenas is a centre-left candidate in the mayoral race.
Before then, a Federal Reserve panel will meet to review U.S. interest rate policy on Tuesday and Wednesday.
"I feel the bourse has fully priced in a Cardenas win and no rate hikes by the FOMC," the trader said, referring to the policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee, or FOMC.
Still, an expected rise in domestic interest rates at Tuesday night's primary auction contributed the decline in share prices Monday, analysts said.

"Dealers see no changes in U.S. base rates from the FOMC.. However, today's orderly profit-taking was a response to predicted increases in Cetes rates tomorrow," said Roberto Galvan, an analyst at the Bursametrica consultancy.
Money market traders said they expected bellwether 28-day Cetes rates to rise by up to 300 basis points on Tuesday.

Rather than selling off their positions, investors were selling outperforming blue chips to buy laggard stocks, Galvan said. "There is still investment in sectors with cheap multiples, like mining and retail," he said.
Mining company Grupo Mexico closed 10 centavos higher at 30.00 pesos, while retail chain Controladora Comercial Mexicana gained 12 centavos to 7.40 pesos.
